name: widen-dealias-ab
description: Timing A/B: do inlinable fast paths for `Type.widen` and `Type.dealias` make serial batch compilation faster? `fastpath-noinl` takes C2's compile-order race on `widen1` out of the picture.
dotc to `-Ystop-after:pickler`, single-shot 30+16, patched JDK 26, 6 forks per variant, interleaved.

variantDescriptions.base: scala/scala3 main `d168df2a76` + library stamps `2cd1ec8c08` (the lab does not build against current main since scala/scala3#27416)
variantDescriptions.fastpath: `Type.widen` and `Type.dealias(keeps)` as small final fronts (class tests only) that C2 can inline at every call site, delegating to private `widen1`/`dealias1` (`a00fcb825d`, cherry-pick of `f573da67cc` from branch `claude/widen-dealias-fastpath-7da49b`)
variantDescriptions.fastpath2: `fastpath`, plus the `dealias` front answers TypeRefs to classes (about half of all `dealias` calls) via `symbol.isClass`; 53 bytes, so inlined only at hot call sites (`6e089e940d`, cherry-pick of `2f4161fca0`)
variantDescriptions.fastpath-noinl: `fastpath`'s build, with `-XX:CompileCommand=dontinline` on `widen1` and `dealias1`, so C2 can never inline the slow paths into the fronts' own compiles: the pilot showed that when `widen1` is inlined into `widen`, `widen`'s nmethod reaches 15 KB and callers refuse it as "already compiled into a big method"
